The EU, as in many of its member states, has a very active and powerful proponent of the GMO (genetically modified organisms, according to them, should be called "innovative" as well) lobby. They say that GMO is a panacea, a silver bullet, a great solution for feeding the world. The EU has approved many GMO products, but every single one of them is a condition: no, or very restricted use, only under very strict limitations, you know, but not monstrosities like open, but only under the conditions, as a rule, modified organisms, a thing, a tool, a pet, a pet food, food, but, as a rule, never as an application on or in human beings. Why? No, no reason. Yes, some, a very limited number of reasons, but not the ones mentioned by the anti-GMO activists. To all those unspoken reasons, I would add the one I'm publishing here, as I observed this for the first time in my awareness of the topic (more than 30 years) now. Mass immigration leads to the need for a large amount of land for growing food, mostly for feed for the ever growing herds of food producing animals. This need for larger and larger areas for the production of food, including feed, is a well known fact. But, there is another kind of food, GMO food, which needs very little space, as it contains mostly plant vs. Animals, both of which, in the process of GMO, the application of genetic engineering, a new, different and very advanced technology is used, the genetic modification of plants, and the modification of animals. GMO plants need less space, and some of the GMO animals need less space as well. But there is also a need for a new, very important and until now unknown area for the application of genetic engineering: the so-called "human enhancement", the genetic modification of humans, which needs space as well. Just like producing food, the need for "human enhancement" leads to a need for larger areas. First of all, there is a need for new, untouched land, for both the production of food and for the application of genetic engineering, including human enhancement. The amount needed, however, can not be determined with full certainty, but a good estimate could be: a little more than 99.9% of the land is needed for food production, and a little more than 0.1% of the land is needed for human enhancement. As the area and the needs for them grow, the estimate for the ratio of food production and human enhancement needs will also change, but it will always keep the proportion mentioned above. So, in the 30 years, the ratio of food production and human enhancement needs will both grow, but the first one will grow faster, so the need for human enhancement will become less and less important. The ratio between food production and human enhancement needs will be more and more balanced, but only for a moment, as the ratio between the needs will shift more and more into the favor of human enhancement. This shift will be faster, as the needs of food production and human enhancement, and as the size of both needs, will grow, but, as I mentioned, the need for food production will always greatly exceed the need for human enhancement. This is true in practice, but it is also true that, as the needs, the growth of the needs and the ratio of the needs are all growing, the ratio between food production and human enhancement needs will become more and more balanced, and this ratio will approach 50:50. But this is the most ideal situation for a 50:50 ratio, in which both needs are the same. This will never be true, as the needs for food production will always exceed the need for human enhancement, but there will be a ratio, and this ratio will also approach 50:50, but the real ratio will always be a little bit further from this point. If the real ratio for food production needs is r, and the ratio for human enhancement needs is 1/r, then, as the ratio approaches 50:50, the ratio r gets closer and closer to 1, and the ratio 1/r gets closer and closer to 1. If the ratio r is 100, then the ratio 1/r is 0.01, if r is 10, then the ratio 1/r is 0.1, and if r is 3, then the ratio 1/r is 0.33. So, as the limit is approached, the ratio r goes to infinity, and the ratio 1/r goes to zero. This means, that the needs for food production will be much greater than the need for human enhancement, and as the limit is approached, this difference will practically approach infinity. So, the proportion of GMO and human genetic engineering is different, and the proportion is very different, as the former will always outnumber the latter by a huge factor.

There are, by the way, many GMO vegetables which have been approved so far, and many of them have been created to resist some specific problems, like pests, harsh weather, and the like. There is a sort of a marketing slogan for the GMOs, and it is something like "the best way to feed the world's growing population is by using the right kind and amount of GMOs". This is more or less the same as for using a corresponding amount, say, 0.1% of organic food, but I'm sure this slogan is just an ordinary one, and not a slogan used by anti-GMO activists. The reason for this is, as I mentioned, that the use of GMOs, especially the ones created to be resistant to a specific herbicide, allows us to solve the problem of the available farmland, but not of the available food. Walt Disney (1909-1966) was an American animator and co-founder of The Walt Disney Company. This section about the story of Walt Disney encompasses his birth, significant decisions, and other major events in his life.

1. Early Life

Walt Disney (1909-1966) was born in Chicago, Illinois, USA. His father, Elias Disney, was a businessman, and his mother, Emma Milford, was an actress. Disney had two older brothers, Herbert and Roy, and a younger sister, Ruth. As a child, Disney was described as a problem child who attended the PS 108 school in the rural area of the Chicago River. A Certified Public Public Accountant (CPA) is a professional who has attained a CPA license, which signifies that the individual meets the requirements for becoming a CPA, which typically include:

1. Education: The first step to becoming a CPA is usually obtaining a college education in accounting, which is typically (but not necessarily) a bachelor's degree in a relevant academic field. The CPA education requirements vary across countries, but in most countries, formal education is just the first step. Almost all universities offer an accounting degree, and many also require students to maintain a certain minimum GPA.

2. CPA license: To become a Certified Public Accountant (CPA), an individual must first meet the requirements for becoming a CPA, which usually include:

- Education: As a first step, an individual in the CPA profession typically needs to earn a bachelor's degree in accounting or a related, relevant field. The CPA education requirements vary by country, but in most countries, a formal education in accounting is typically required.

- Exam: After completing an undergraduate degree in accounting, the next step is to obtain the CPA certification, which requires meeting certain educational requirements and passing the CPA exam. The education requirements and the exam requirements may vary by country, but in most countries, becoming a CPA typically involves obtaining an accounting degree, and passing the necessary exams and meeting any other requirements.

3. Meeting requirements: In addition to meeting the educational and exam requirements, there may be other requirements for becoming a CPA, which typically include:

- Continuing education: Continuing education is usually required to maintain an active CPA certification.

CPAs who become certified usually have no idea what an CPA designation is, as these are the qualifications and certification for becoming a Certified Public Accountant. A Certified Public Accountant (CPA) are typically based in their local area. The S&P 500 is one of the most popular and widely recognized stock market indices in the world. It is a free float market capitalization weighted index, meaning the component stocks are weighted by the number of shares available in the free float. As such, the S&P 500’s composition is not static, and changes in the form of additions and deletions can have a noticeable effect on the index. This is because the S&P 500 is a market capitalization weighted index, which means that the larger the proportion of a company’s free float, the higher the weight it carries in the index. To understand the impact of a company on the S&P 500, we will take an example and examine a hypothetical scenario in which Microsoft (MSFT) is added to the S&P 500.

How to show featured posts using PHP. In this tutorial, I’ll show you how to display featured content using PHP. In the code below, I’m showing you a sample database with some sample content.

Sample database:

Table: posts

| id | title | content | type |
| -- | ----- | ------- | ---- |
| 1  | Post 1 | ... |  |
| 2  | Post 2 | ... |  |
| 3  | Post 3 | ... |  |

Table: featured_posts

| id | post_id | post_type | order |
| -- | ------- | --------- | ----- |
| 1  | 1       | 1         | 1     |
| 2  | 2       | 2         | 2     |

As you can see, there’s no featured post type in the above example. This is just to demonstrate how to display featured content, even if you don’t have a featured post.

To show featured data, you’ll need the ID of the featured content. If you have to display the content of current featured post on a different page, you’ll need two things:

You’ll get the current page using the following code. In this example, I’m assuming you’re using the default PHP configuration.

In this example, we have two pages. The first one is the home page, and the second one is a single post.

The home page will display the three latest featured content, and the single post page will display the selected latest featured content.

If you want to show featured content on a page, get the IDs using this SQL:

```
SELECT post_ID, post_type_ID FROM featured_content
WHERE order_num = 'Display index page' AND featured_post_type IS NOT NULL
```

If you want to show featured content on a page, and the featured content is a post from a category, get the IDs using this SQL:

```
SELECT post_ID, post_type_ID FROM 
  (SELECT post_ID, post_type_ID, MAX(post_category_ID) AS catID
  FROM featured_content 
  WHERE post_category_type IS NOT NULL 
  GROUP BY post_type_ID) sub
WHERE sub.post_ID LIKE 'featured_to_post_%' OR (sub.post_ID = 'featured_post' AND sub.catID = 'post' AND sub.post_type_ID = 123);
```

If you don’t want to show the featured content, but just the featured content’s fields, use this SQL:

```
SELECT p.post_ID, p.post_type_ID AS post_type, p.title AS title, p.content AS content, p.date_published AS date_published, p.author_ID AS author, ft.post_type_ID AS type, ft.order_num AS post_order
FROM posts p

This is not because you need to learn SQL, please start into SQL. Whether you look at implementation of SQL, algorithms, models, methodologies, best practices, online ressources for SQL, you will find that many, many, many times, the term "ETL" or "data integration" is mentioned.

What is ETL? ETL is the common term for "Extract, Transform, and Load. The term ETL was popular in the '90 when EDI was used to exchange data between business processes. Nowadays, the term is used in relational databases, and the reason is simple: with ETL, even if you have two identical sets of data in your database, there might have a need to just perform some ETL.

If you are a database developer, who is developing with SQL, you will do this job. If you develop a data migration project, you will use tools. You will use SQL development, design tools, but you will also need a version comparison tool, but you know this. If you have read my article about dev, you know what I described there. But if you need to know ETL tools, two kind of solutions, there are two different strategies, there are two things to know: one is the features, the other is the licensing.

There are two facets: the features and the licensing.

1. Features

This are the two features that a data comparison and data migration (but data migration tools are much more than that; the two features are part of the feature set):

1.1 Speed: How fast can the tool compare two sets of data (left, and right, where left is the database on the left, and right is the database on the right) in a given system with data and a given hardware?

1.2 Features: What does the data comparison tool provide, what are the functions of the data migration and data comparison tool? Here follow the most important (except for the speed, I'll try to sort these by popularity):

1.1 Performance: Both tools need to be fast.

1.2 Openness: If you add a data migration suite, you will have different sources, like SQL, CSV, JSON, PDF, XML, …, the more you support, the better.

1.3 Ease of use: The tool should be easy to use.

1.4 Portability: If you have a Windows tool, how many platforms does it support?

1.5 Flexibility: The solution should be flexible in terms of licensing, you can choose a license that fits you, and you're not forced to a specific license model.

1.6 Support: There should be a way to get support, like a knowledge base, documentation, support forum or even personal support.

1.7 Migrations: The better the tool migrates, the better. A good data migration solution should be able to migrate the data, the schema, the security, the users, the permissions, …

1.8 Automation: The higher the degree of automation, the more you save time.

1.9 Script: A script to execute should be provided to verify the results of the migration.

1.10 Performance: A high performance is important, the faster the better.

Now, let's look at the different vendors for data migration and comparison solutions. The following (except the, let's say, less than 1% of other solutions) are either self-developed solutions, or they use a proprietary solution which is based on a third party solution.

To show how to beat a vendor, let's have a look on the market and a couple of the companies and skip the many where I would write only what I already wrote:

1. Position, who offers the best SQL tool?

If you compare the features Microsoft delivers with SQL Server, SQL, Data Integraiton, with the competition, you will see that Microsoft is ahead. If you compare the implementation, Microsoft is again better. If you see a 3rd system, maybe performance (plus the better Microsoft is still the competition) and features, but the competition is lacking a lot behind.

If you compare the features of SQL Server 2016 with the competition, you will see that Microsoft is ahead. If you compare the implementation, you'll see that Microsoft is ahead again, and the competition is still behind.

Now, the best way to show how to compare two is to do an example. I took two very popular RDBMS, with this setup, I applied a data comparison, the result was one point, I do not remember the points, but the first one has a positive better result, and the second one has a lower result. We set up the first RDBMS in 1998, and the second in 2018. The test was done on both of them, and we found that the first RDBMS is 20 years, and the second one is 2 years old. So, we saved 20 years, and this is huge.

Let's compare SQL Server 2018 with 2017, 2016, 2015, 2014, 2012, 2008 R2, 2008, 2005, 2000, SQL Server 7, SQL Server 6.5, and before that, we used different solutions. Let's assume that in this 22 years, we created a lot of SQL Server databases, and we migrated among them a lot. If we look at the feature, we can see that SQL 7 was not supporting always T-SQL, but this is a very long time. So, SQL 2018 has added a lot of features to the language in the last 22 years, and this is great. Now, if you use the same T-SQL dialect from 1996 until 2018, you will have a hard time, and it will be nearly impossible to support all the other features, and this is the reason, that with each new SQL Server version, Microsoft SQL, and with it, data comparison and data migration tools, had to evolve.

Now, if a new SQL Server version comes up, it will not only bring new features, but also improve the existing ones, and this is a good thing. Looking to the future, we will have the Internet of Things, AI, 5G, and new SQL Server. Let's see, how much features they will add and improve, and how fast data integration and data migration tools will follow.

2. Licensing

Now, the second aspect is the licensing. If you have a close look on the different SQL servers, and you compare their licensing, you will find 3 models:

1. Perpetual license - This is an license, where you pay once, and the SQL Server is yours. You can use it forever. You will get upgrades (usually not extra), but also support (usually not for free). Microsoft offers this for a high price, and there are a few others, like Oracle, who offer this for an extremely high price.

2. Term license - This is a license, where you pay for 1-3 years, and at the end of the term, you need to buy a new license. This is called a rental, and you need to pay every year. Microsoft offers this for a lower price, and this is the only way to get support for SQL Server, if you have a significantly cheaper solution.

3. Cloud Solution - This is not a license, where you pay for the live Microsoft, but a usage, like a cloud based solution. You don't get a permanent, but a temporary SQL Server. This is a new thing, and Microsoft offers this for a low price, and the price is also depending on how much you use it.

Now, if you are used to a perpetual license, and you didn't have to worry about expiration, and you had support, the third licensing model is a problem. It is a problem, because you have to care about expiration, and you have to renew, and you don't get support, except you renew. This means, you will have to pay, at least once a year, for the pleasure to use this product.

Let's talk a bit about the cloud solutions. If you are not yet using cloud solutions, you don't need to care much, but it will affect you sooner or later. If you are using cloud solutions, you need a strategy, a plan, and the tools to handle it. If you don't plan, someone else will plan for you, and you will be just a user, and you will find problems, and you will need a support, and you will pay it - per year.

So, if you have a SQL Server, and you look to the future, or even if you are working now with a cloud solution, you should align with the tools, and talk to your manager, and ask for a data migration and comparison solution, and the licensing, to free some money to buy a data migration

Ein Mann besitzt ein ziemlich altes Auto, das 2.000 $ wert ist.
Er hat ein gebrauchtes Auto gesehen, das 8.000 $ wert ist. Er möchte sein altes Auto behalten, bis er sich ein gebrauchtes kaufen kann.
Er glaubt, dass er jeden Monat 1.000 $ sparen kann, aber die Preise seines alten
Autos und des neuen sinken jeden Monat um 1,5 Prozent.
Außerdem erhöht sich dieser Verlustprozentsatz um 0,5 Prozent.
Unserem Mann fallen all diese Berechnungen schwer.
Können Sie ihm helfen?
Wie viele Monate wird er brauchen, um genug Geld zu sparen, um sich das Auto seiner Wahl zu kaufen,
und wie viel Geld wird ihm übrig bleiben?

Yes, there are free Software Assurance (SAST) tools. Software Assurance (also known as Software Verification) is the field of applying structured or formal methods to determine the quality and reliability of software. SAST tools support automated verification of software by analyzing code using various static analysis techniques.

1. The term "free and open-source software assurance" (FOSD) describes the use of software assurance techniques, including techniques used in proprietary software, but made freely available for wider and more established use.

2. When examining and detecting indicators of quality and reliability issues in software, it may be helpful to refer to the name of the software in relation to the fact, such as in:

- Software reliability: There is little a software expert can do to ensure software reliability. A software developer can, however, learn from software assurance and apply software testing methods to create software.

- Awareness: As for the level of awareness, software developers need to know at a minimum, some or certain core requirements to introduce software assurance early in the software development process. For instance, fully implementing code quality metrics will greatly help.

- Software developers: To develop reliable software, when developers develop a new, you can leverage best practices. Otherwise, if you are developing a new, it may be a good idea to start from scratch.

3. Many software products come with SAST. For software using some form of SAST, there are also free alternatives. Free SAST tools, while often having limited features.

3. As free software SAST, typically have limited features. There are also initiatives that provide resources, such as SAST communities.

Using a descriptive, narrative style, and a vivid, engaging voice, have the protagonist go on an adventure to find her lost sister. As you write, create a unique and consistent world, and include at least five instances of dialogue that reveal the characters' personalities and relationships.

In the dream, Emma heard a shriek that split the night. It was her sister, Anna, and the scream was full of terror. Emma's heart raced, and she awoke, gasping for air. She looked around, disoriented. The sun had set without her notice, and the bungalow was draped in the shadows of an unfamiliar night.

Emma had not seen her sister, Anna, for days. Emma assumed her hunting expedition in the dense, jungle-like woods behind their house. Anna studied paleontology, and had found a rare opportunity to observe dinosaurs in their natural habitat. Emma hadn't been worried at first, but when Anna didn't return, her confidence waned.

Dinosaurs in the wild were dangerous, and Anna, without her rifle, had very little chance against a T-Rex or a Stegosaurus. Emma's heart sank at the thought of her sister, a defenseless human, being prey to the fearsome Tyrant. She quickly donned a backpack with supplies, and set out to find her sister.

In the dream, Emma had followed a brook that wound through the jungle, but the soundscape of birds and rustling ferns had given way to the screech of a Strigiformes. She opened her eyes, and the world outside her window was cloaked in shadows. The dream had not vanished, however, the sound of the owl was more vivid.

Emma stepped out of the house, and the humid air wrapped around her like a thick blanket. Fireflies, like glowing embers, flickered among the ferns, but their light was outshone by the pulsing bioluminescence of the mushroom caps that lined the jungle floor. Strange plants of every size, shape, and color grew so densely, their leaves brushed past her as the thick underbrush snaked around her legs.

The dream was so real, she barely recognized it as such. This was no normal nightmare, and when she tried to walk, she stumbled over the uneven terrain. The jungle was a giant, living thing, with tangled vines that snaked around her ankles, and prickly bushes that raked her arms. The smell of petrichor was overwhelmed by the scent of rot, and she gagged.

She had to find a way out, but the walls of the jungle pressed in on her, and the sky was a sunless expanse. She had to keep moving, put one foot in front of the other, and search for her sister. The jungle was haunted, and the ghosts were the creatures she had known in the other world.

A large, scaly tail slapped the ground, and Emma froze. A Stegosaurus, and it was getting closer. She had to get out of sight. She turned, and her boot hit a protruding rock. She tumbled, and a hand found a patch of moss. It slowed her descent, but she still landed hard on her side. Her backpack, which she had clutched tightly, spilled its contents: a hunting knife, a small canteen, a map, and a compass.

She clutched the knife, and rose, ready to confront the dinosaur. But when she saw the Stegosaurus, her mind went blank. She had to get back to the house, to think. The dream, or whatever it was, was too real to be ignored.

Her steps, at first, were sure, but as she walked, her confidence waned. The Stegosaurus was between her and the house, and she had to get by it without alerting it. She moved as silently as she could, but the underbrush, in a sudden panic, swished and crackled.

In the recent years, I published more than 600 articles in this website, about 130 of them are in my "Web Design and HTML" category, which means they are about HTML, and they cover a lot of general concepts, a lot of basic things, a lot of things, but also some important differences. Here are the 3 articles you need, but I guess you don't have to go through them all, I had several articles about HTML, HTML5, and CSS: here are 3 of them:

1. How to make your website look more modern
2. HTML5 Canvas vs. HTML5 SVG: which one to use?
3. HTML5 Drag and Drop, HTML as UI

When you create websites, there are many other things you can use to make them more appealing, and a good way is to make them look modern. A website that looks old, slow, and outdated is not something you want these days, because there are tools and technologies that make it possible to create something more than the old websites. Here are a few tips to make your website look more modern:

1. Use the latest CSS framework
There are many CSS frameworks out there, some of them are very old, while others are more recent. If you want a modern look, you need a modern CSS framework. Some popular ones are Bootstrap, Foundation, Materialize, Semantic UI, and so on.

2. Use responsive design
With responsive design, your website will look good on all screen sizes, from small mobile devices to large screens. In the past, websites that looked good on larger screens were broken on smaller screens, and vice versa. If your website looks bad on a small screen, it looks outdated.

3. Use the latest HTML
Using the latest HTML (HTML5) is better than using older versions. It is easier to use, supported by all major browsers, and there are a lot of tools that make web development faster.

4. Use the right CSS
Using the latest CSS is a better choice than older ones. Using CSS3, instead of its older version, CSS 2, makes your website look more modern. Some old stuff is still in CSS3, but you can use the newer stuff, too.

5. Use JavaScript
If you want to make your website more interactive, you need to use JavaScript. Old websites were static, but with JavaScript, you can make your website dynamic. There's also a new trend, called Single Page Application, that is created with JavaScript, and show in the client on the user's browser.

6. Use the Document Object Model (DOM)
The Document Object Model (DOM) is a standard used by JavaScript, which describes the way of accessing documents, such as HTML. The DOM is a W3C standard, and the latest one is the DOM5.0. There are a few specifications that are on the way to becoming recommendations, too. If you want to use the latest JavaScript, you should use the latest DOM.

7. Choose the right JavaScript
JavaScript has also gone through many changes, and using the latest one, ECMAScript 2018, is always a better choice than older versions. It's a better choice to use the latest one, because it makes your website look more modern, and it's also easier to use, and there are a lot of new tools that make web development faster.

8. Choose a fast loading website
A fast loading website is essential, because the internet is fast, and users can find other websites if yours is not fast. To make your website load faster, you can use a content delivery network (CDN), cache your website, minify your HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, and so on.

9. Use a performance oriented workflow
To make your website perform better, you need a performance oriented workflow. You need to use the right tools, and there are a lot of them. Some are old, and some are new, but you should try to use the latest ones, because they make your work faster, and your website better.

10. Use a performance oriented web host
To make your website load faster, it's not only the website itself that needs to be optimized, but also the web host. There are web hosts that are optimized for performance, and some that are not. If you want your website to be more modern, you should choose a performance oriented web host.

11. Use a fast web server
Most of the work a web server does, is to serve the content, which means that a fast web server, like Nginx, can make your website load faster, and your web host should use a fast web server.

12. Use a content delivery network (CDN)
A content delivery network (CDN) is a group of servers, distributed all over the world. When a user requests a file (for example, an HTML file), the server that is closest to the user serves that file. When the most distant server is used, the file needs more time to get to the user, but with a CDN, the file is served by a nearby server, which means that the file gets to the user more quickly. A CDN minimizes the page load time, and a faster website is always better than a slower one.

13. Use HTTP/2
HTTP/1.1, the old version of HTTP, makes a website slower, because it can only download one file at a time. HTTP/2, the latest version, allows for multiple files to be downloaded at the same time. With HTTP/2, your web pages load faster, and your users are happier.

14. Use AMP, to make your website load faster
AMP, or Accelerated Mobile Pages, is a web framework, especially made for mobile phones. It significantly speeds up your website, but the price to pay is the limited flexibility, because not all features of a regular website are available in an AMP website.

15. Use a resource: Unheap
Unheap is a website, which can help you save time, and make the best use of your time, by saving you the effort of finding, reading, and understanding about the state of the art JavaScript (ECMAScript) tools. The website is not a plugin or a library, but only a collection of tools, so you can find the tool that suits you the best. You can use the search, browse the tools, or read the articles to find the tools that can help you save time, and make your web development faster, and, as a result, your websites better.

Among these new ideas, which would shape the future, the most important was, according to Herzen, the idea of freedom. Herzen's essay was a philosophical meditation, but a contemporary of his, the Swiss historian and jurist Jacob Burckhardt, also dealt with the same issues, and like Herzen, he also saw the "new ideas" as representing freedom. Historic dramas (also historic films and plays) are dramatic works based on historical events. The term typically denotes works where the focus, emphasis, and major elements of the work are historical events. Historic dramas are distinguished from other types of dramas (or more general dramatic works) by the particular historical events that are their focus. The form of these works is often related to film or theater, but the methods of presentation (in film and theater) differ from the categorization of these works.

The scope of historic dramas covers the entire span of historical works in which the quality of the historical events as historically true is important. In contrast, the scope of works in related categories is generally broader. Historic dramas (as a category) often include works in which no specific historical event is known as being in the category, but rather a general notional idea about historical events.

There is a tradition of dramatic and cinematic works that are not specifically focused on particular events, but simply depict the general nature of historical events as they are, often exaggerating the importance of certain features and details. These are not, however, biographical works about famous or significant historical figures, but works that are focused on the genre as a whole.

In the 19th century, dramatic and literary works appeared that focused on the inner lives of characters, often emphasizing the power of fiction, the importance of individual subjectivity, and the social sciences. Many such works used the new era's version of the word's always-been-familiar devices, such as the use of free form, first-person point of view, and subjective and objective narration, but what set these apart was their focus on the study of history and the world itself. This period, known as the Age of History, saw the same general trends as those that had preceded them, but in the wake of the previous centuries, they were well-recorded and well-understood.

Subject: Request for job salary range

Title: The Cosmic Quantum Fields—and the Animals of Quantum Physics

Author: Helge Kragh (University of Aarhus, Denmark)

In 1913, Niels Bohr published his famous quantum paper, which, he said, “contains the germ of a fundamental revolution in our understanding of the structure of atoms.” Bohr is credited with launching the new quantum theory, but, according to Helge Kragh, his contribution has been widely misunderstood. Kragh, a historian of science, argues in his excellent book that Bohr’s “germ” was not a complete proposal for quantum mechanics, as is almost universally believed, but a hypothesis for what we now call quantum field theory, the field that investigates the deep structures and fundamental nature of the universe. Bohr is rightly regarded as a most influential founder of quantum mechanics, but his 1913 paper was not about quantum mechanics. The 1913 paper was a proposal for what Kragh calls “quantum-field mending,” a theory for reconciling two of the four known forces that govern the universe: the electromagnetic force and the weak nuclear force. The latter force, a sub-atomic force that governs certain types of radioactive decay, so far had confounded theorists. It was observed as a phenomenon, but its cause was not well understood. Bohr proposed that this force, and the electromagnetic force, were expressions of a single underlying phenomenon, “quantum jumps” in atoms, and that the apparent separation of the forces was due to the “mending” or “healing” of the universe in its efforts to suppress the display of quantum phenomena. The idea seems bizarre, but Kragh shows that it was a well-considered and rational hypothesis, given the state of physics at the time. Bohr’s “quantum-field mending” was not fully developed, and the idea was largely ignored. It took many years, even decades, before the deep forces and the underlying particles that govern the universe, including the weak nuclear force, could be investigated and understood using better experimental techniques and more powerful theories. By the 1940s, the necessary tools were available, and the field of quantum field theory began to take shape. Kragh shows that Bohr’s 1913 paper was a foreshadowing of the new field, but for nearly 80 years, Bohr’s hypothesis lay forgotten, overlooked by later physicists and historians, who read into Bohr’s paper only a germ for quantum mechanics. Kragh says that Bohr’s “quantum-field mending” was best forgotten, and that Bohr was right to “forget” his hypothesis, for it was not developed enough to be taken seriously on its own. However, the hypothesis, though not fully explained, contained some important ideas. Kragh says that it is time for another “remembering” of Bohr’s 1913 paper, this time, not just for its ideas on quantum mechanics, but for the new idea, “quantum-field mending.” This remembering, says Kragh, does not deny the importance of Bohr’s contributions to the foundation of quantum mechanics, but it does reevaluate Bohr’s legacy and the extent of his influence on 20th century physics.

Sie erhalten einige Kritiken zu einem Film. In jedem Video werden möglicherweise einige negative oder positive Punkte über den Film erwähnt. Lesen Sie sie sorgfältig durch und ziehen Sie die positiven und negativen Punkte heraus, die in allen Kritiken erwähnt werden. Erstellen Sie dann eine Liste dieser Punkte und fassen Sie sie als positive und negative Punkte zusammen.

Kritik 1: Ich bin mir nicht sicher, ob es nur daran liegt, dass Ed Norton in diesem Film wirklich auf die Nerven geht, aber ich habe nie wirklich an die Idee geglaubt, dass Fight Club eine Art kulturelles Phänomen ist. Ja, es ist eine innovative Geschichte, erzählt durch ein starkes Drehbuch, fesselnde Charaktere und intensive Kinematographie. Aber ist sie wirklich so viel Lob wert? Ich persönlich finde, dass sie auf halbem Weg auseinanderfällt und gegen Ende tatsächlich ziemlich langweilig wird. Alles wird einfach ein bisschen kindisch und konstruiert, da die Geschichte den Kontakt zu ihren Grundelementen verliert und die Stimmung der Wut gegen die Maschine überhand nimmt. Ich habe großen Respekt vor der Art und Weise, wie dieser Film gemacht wurde, aber ähnlich wie bei Matrix habe ich das Gefühl, dass die Leute diesem Film viel mehr Bedeutung beimessen, als er verdient.
Kritik 2: Der Film erzählt die Geschichte von Männern, die sich nicht an die soziale Ordnung der heutigen Welt anpassen können und unter der Führung von Tyler Durden ihren natürlichen Instinkt, ihre Männlichkeit, entdecken und ihrem unglücklichen Leben entkommen.
Kritik 3: Trotz eines guten Themas, großartiger Schauspielerei und wichtiger Botschaften, die dieser Film auf unorthodoxe Weise vermittelt, schafft er es meiner Meinung nach nicht, das Publikum mit der Handlung zu verbinden, und lässt es in einer Welt der Verwirrung zurück. Obwohl die Mehrheit der Kritiker diesen Film unterhaltsam und interessant findet, würde ich mich dennoch zu der Minderheit zählen, die glaubt, dass dieser Film extrem überbewertet ist.
Kritik 4: Ist das Schaffen von Chaos, Explosionen und die Mitgliedschaft in einer militanten Sekte der Weg, um materielle Fesseln loszuwerden?! Die visuellen Effekte sind faszinierend und die Geschichte ist bis zur zweiten Hälfte fesselnd. Leider endet sie nicht gut.

Fassen Sie den Artikel, den Sie erhalten haben, kurz zusammen.

Mathematik und Kunst sind auf verschiedene Weise miteinander verbunden. Mathematik selbst wird als eine von Schönheit motivierte Kunst beschrieben. Mathematik findet sich in Künsten wie Musik, Tanz, Malerei, Architektur, Bildhauerei und Textilien. Dieser Artikel konzentriert sich jedoch auf Mathematik in den bildenden Künsten.
Mathematik und Kunst haben eine lange historische Beziehung. Künstler verwenden Mathematik seit dem 4. Jahrhundert v. Chr., als der griechische Bildhauer Polyklet seinen Kanon schrieb, in dem er Proportionen vorschrieb, die vermutlich auf dem Verhältnis 1:√2 für den idealen männlichen Akt basierten. Es gibt hartnäckige populäre Behauptungen über die Verwendung des Goldenen Schnitts in der antiken Kunst und Architektur, ohne dass es zuverlässige Beweise dafür gibt. In der italienischen Renaissance schrieb Luca Pacioli die einflussreiche Abhandlung De divina proportione (1509), illustriert mit Holzschnitten von Leonardo da Vinci, über die Verwendung des Goldenen Schnitts in der Kunst. Ein anderer italienischer Maler, Piero della Francesca, entwickelte Euklids Ideen zur Perspektive in Abhandlungen wie De Prospectiva Pingendi und in seinen Gemälden weiter. Der Kupferstecher Albrecht Dürer nahm in seinem Werk Melencolia I viele Bezüge zur Mathematik auf. In der Neuzeit machte der Grafiker M. C. Escher mit Hilfe des Mathematikers H. S. M. Coxeter intensiven Gebrauch von Tessellation und hyperbolischer Geometrie, während die De-Stijl-Bewegung unter der Führung von Theo van Doesburg und Piet Mondrian ausdrücklich geometrische Formen aufgriff. Die Mathematik hat Textilkünste wie Quilten, Stricken, Kreuzstich, Häkeln, Sticken, Weben, türkische und andere Teppichherstellung sowie Kelim inspiriert. In der islamischen Kunst zeigen sich Symmetrien in so unterschiedlichen Formen wie persischen Girih- und marokkanischen Zellige-Fliesenarbeiten, durchbrochenen Steinschirmen im Mogul-Jali-Stil und weit verbreiteten Muqarnas-Gewölben.

Title: The Master Book of the Middle Ages: An Illustrated Encyclopedia, 2 vols., 1965, by George Fischer. [LCCN 64-20568]

This work, a compilation of brief articles on an array of medieval topics, is accompanied by numerous illustrations, including 160 in volume one. The illustrations are accompanied by introductory text (often three elided words) and titles. They are frequently well-researched, well-executed, and of high quality. The quality of the entries depends, naturally, upon the introductory text. The following is a selected, random sample, as intended to illustrate the considerable range of this work to a modern reader.

1. Abbot: A man who, in a monastery, ranks next below the abbot abbot general. Abots, also called fathers, must be of lawful age and must have a knowledge of the Holy Writ. They can be clerics, but most of them are laymen. They live in a separate building, which must have a chapel.

2. Abbacy: A tenancy, or the right to hold the office of abbot.

3. Abbacy Nullius: A Benedictine abbacy that is subject to the Holy See, not to a bishop.

4. Abbey: A monastery of canons, who are priests, or of Benedictine monks, who are not priests, but who lead a life of prayer and work. The term is also applied to a monastery of nuns.

5. Abbey-Douro: A monastery at Saintes, in the modern French department of Charente, in Aquitaine. It was an abbey of canons, and was founded about 560.

6. Abbots: See Bishops.

7. Abbots of St. Albans: An hereditary abbacy, in which the abbots of St. Albans were successors to the abbey’s founder, Herbert, and held their office by hereditary right. The first abbot was elected about 1077; the last, Richard de Bungey, was deposed in 1172. Thereafter, the abbacy was held by members of the de Warrenne family, who were successors to Herbert in the manor of Sarratt, and who held the office by hereditary right.

8. Abbots of Tewkesbury: An hereditary abbacy, in which the abbots of Tewkesbury were successors to the abbey’s founder, Osric, and held their office by hereditary right. The first abbot was elected in 715; the last, Robert, was deposed in 1102. Thereafter, the abbacy was held by members of the Fitzharding family, who were successors to the last abbot in the earldom of Gloucester, and who held the office by hereditary right. The first of the family to be abbot was Richard, who was appointed in 1108.

9. Abbots, Gilbert of Lire: The 12th century abbot of St. Mary’s Abbey, Lire, in the modern English county of Hants. He was appointed about 1172; he was succeeded in 1177 by his brother, Richard.

10. Abbots, Richard of Lire: The 12th century abbot of St. Mary’s Abbey, Lire, in the modern English county of Hants. He succeeded his brother, Gilbert, in 1177; he was succeeded in 1189 by his kinsman, William.

11. Abbots, Robert of Tewkesbury: The last of the hereditary abbots of Tewkesbury. He was deposed in 1102, and the abbey was thereafter held by members of the Fitzharding family, who were also earls of Gloucester.

12. Abbots, Roger of Battle: The 13th century abbot of Battle, in the modern English county of Sussex. He was appointed about 1206; he was succeeded in 1218 by his kinsman, William.

13. Abbots, Roger of Newminster: The 13th century abbot of Newminster, in the modern English county of Northumberland. He was appointed in 1216; he was succeeded in 1233 by John.

14. Abbots, Roger of Peterborough: The 13th century abbot of Peterborough, in the modern English county of Cambridgeshire. He was appointed about 1202; he was succeeded in 1239 by Thomas.

15. Abbots, Thomas of Tewkesbury: A Benedictine, the 13th century abbot of Tewkesbury, in the modern English county of Glos. He was appointed in 1239; he was appointed the abbey’s cellarer, and held that office from 1216 to 1235.

16. Abbots, Walter of Evesham: The 13th century abbot of Evesham, in the modern English county of Worcs. He was appointed in 1244; he was succeeded in 1258 by William.

17. Abbots, William of Battle: A Benedictine, the 13th century abbot of Battle, in the modern English county of Sussex. He was appointed in 1218; he was a poet, and he wrote a verse life of his predecessor, Richard, and a metrical history of the kings of England.

18. Abbots, William of Peterborough: The 13th century abbot of Peterborough, in the modern English county of Cambridgeshire. He was appointed in 1239; he wrote a chronicle, which covered the history of the abbey and the English nation.

19. Abbots, William of Tewkesbury: A Benedictine, the 13th century abbot of Tewkesbury, in the modern English county of Glos. He was appointed in 1258; he was a poet, and he wrote a metrical life of St. William.

20. Abbot Samson: A Benedictine, the 13th century abbot of St. Edmunds, in the modern English county of Suffolk. He entered the abbey as a lay brother, and served as its cellarer and almoner. He was elected abbot of St. Edmunds in 1211; he ruled with great energy, and was successful in increasing the wealth and power of the abbey.

The Hamburger Bahnhof, Berlin's most considerable museum, is showing the first large retrospective in Germany of contemporary British art: "States of Mind. Alternative Images, Material Culture and Experimental Narratives from the Early 21st Century - British Art Worlds and the Global Contemporary". The exhibition is based on the research project "States of Mind. 1990 - 2010 - British Art and the Global Contemporary" and has found its answer in "Alternativity: The Moon and Beyond". The show is curated by Katrin Pesch, Dirk Nishen, and Mark Hallett. Until January 6th, 2019, a collection of 56 contemporary artworks will be presented in the Museum of Applied Arts, Vienna. The exhibition is organized in partnership with the Coventry UK City of Culture. "States of Mind" will travel to 5 partner venues through the UK. The first, "States of Mind: 1990-2010, British Art and the Global Contemporary" has exhibited in Birmingham and will tour the UK in 2018. The second, "Alternativity: The Moon and Beyond" has already traveled to previous shows and is now, aged, part of the collection. The exhibition has been held in Budapest, Germany, and is moving from country to country. The next show will be in Edinburgh, the following one in London, and after that, the show will be in the large cities in the British Crown colonies: Delhi, Singapore, Dubai, and at the end, the capital of the mother land, Canterbury, which is yet hosting the "States of Mind" project for a few more months. The third and upcoming exhibition, "The Palace of the Republic: 1976-1990, East-Central European Art in an Inter-European and Global Context" is held in Berlin, and is a different story. The exhibition will be in Berlin until the 6th of January, 2019, and the visitors might find it quite interesting, as it closes with the opening of the curtains on the art scene in Eastern Europe. Lovers will see the exhibitions "States of Mind" and "The Palace of the Republic" as a confirmation of their beliefs, and they will probably find a lot of common ground: both addressed the fall of communism. However, the Hungarian and German curators had different opinions about how to handle their exhibitions. While "States of Mind" showed the aftermath of the social and political changes, "The Palace of the Republic" focused on the period before. The two exhibitions were a good chance to have a look at works from both exhibitions, a comparison of the two a must. But I couldn't make a comparison, as both exhibitions were held in two separate countries: "States of Mind" in the UK, and "The Palace of the Republic" in Germany. The first, "States of Mind", shows 56 contemporary artworks, while the second, "The Palace of the Republic", has 150. The German "States of Mind" curator, Mark Hallett, could not go on a trip to Hungary to see "The Palace of the Republic", but both works are connected by Katrin Stransky, a post-doctoral assistant in the "States of Mind" team. She did some ground planning, and the title says it all: "A Revolution of Images" could have been the title of her thesis as well. She was the link, then, between the two curators, but also between the two countries. Hallett and Pesch could have exchanged ideas and art works, and most likely did, as they were in contact, and the UK and Germany have a good relationship. But the fact remains, that "States of Mind" and "The Palace of the Republic" were exhibitions on the same subject, in two different countries. I am not sure, if this happened for the first time in history, but if so, it's a pity, all that time and that money spent, just for 56 artworks in Birmingham, and 150 in Berlin - what a harsh blow, and the whole with a budget of 1,2 Million Euros. The message, however, is not new, and may have already reached the curators, for the exhibitions were a good opportunity to show that, in the age of globalization, you don't need a treaty to coordinate contemporary art. The reason is, as mentioned, the fall of the Iron Curtain. The curators could have invited each other, but not to plan a co-operation, as the long-distance e-mails would have needed for that, would have taken too long, and the money for plane and hotel, well, it has been "cut" (deleted) from their budgets. So, they couldn't invite, and they also couldn't travel, and all that for political reasons. But even in the absence of an international wall between England and Germany, it is a pity, that the curators have not seen each other's exhibitions, and all that, just for any wall, be it an international one, a national one, or just an inner, mental one. Not to mention all the other, small, local, or individual borders, a product of selfishness, ignorance, and stupidity. Almost every time this is the case, I mention the German art blog, and I realize, unfortunately, that I have to do it again, and this time, even have to mention the blog: The "Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung" has an article, in its Arts section, on the "States of Mind" exhibition, and not by mistake. Herewith, I don't have to, and won't, repeat what has already been said, and shown. I also would like to remind the readers, that the "Galerie Perrotin" in New York is also owned by the French, as I mentioned at the beginning of this post. So "States of Mind" is a Franco-British-German- American art show, well, no, it isn't, it's just a British-German exhibition, and the "Imperium" part is the Canadian part, well, no, it's only a British-German- American show, and the "continent" part is the Italian one, as well, no, it's not, it's just a British-German exhibition, and the "Anglo" part is the Scottish one. So, I don't know how to entitle the title of the exhibition, but it definitely has nothing to do with the one in Düsseldorf. And then, of course, there is also the reverse possibility, to look at the "Palace of the Republic" through the eyes of the British curators, as they did, of course. But, to make it clear, this is not the same, but a similar, no, not similar, but related, no, not related, but another one, no, just a connected, abstract "States of Mind". The "Palace of the Republic" in Berlin, and the one in Budapest, are not the same, even if they deal with similar subjects, but from different points of view, with different art, and a different focus. And "States of Mind" is not a copy of "The Palace of the Republic", but a completely new one. It's like both the same, and also not. So, it would be best to think about the "States of Mind" as two different, and two (Euro)Atlantic, exhibitions, and not to bother with the "similarities". But, it should not come as a surprise, per chance, that the two curators, Hallett, and Pesch, decided to organize two exhibitions with the same title, and almost the same, and a similar theme: "States of Mind. Alternative Images, Material Culture, and Experimental Narratives from the Early 21st Century - British Art Worlds and the Global Contemporary". This means, they divided the artists and artworks, and put them into two, more or less, regions: the British and Irish, and the German and Austrian. This is a natural, and obvious step, as the artists are, in most cases, either clearly from one of these regions, or, in a sense, represent them. But, at the same time, what was the point of this division, and the transatlantic, as well as the European, and even global overtones, if they decided to organize two exhibitions on both sides of the Rhine? The point is, indeed, the artists, and the artworks, and their common theme, but, as the two exhibitions are on both sides of the Rhine, they lost the most important part, the artworks, which are in the other, opposite, or, respectively, the neighboring, region. For example, there is a German art piece, "The Sewing Table" (1973), by Dorothy Alexander, which is not in the "States of Mind", but it should have been, as it fits the theme, and Alexander was a British artist. The same, of course, can be said for the absence of the "Fragment of a Woman's Dress" (1981) by Eileen Agar, which is, somehow, not in the exhibition, although it should have been, as it fits the theme, and Agar was a British artist, as well. Geben Sie eine kurze Erklärung des gewünschten Teils des Dokuments.

Dokument: Die vorherrschenden Sequenztransduktionsmodelle basieren auf komplexen rekurrierenden oder konvolutionellen neuronalen Netzwerken, die einen Encoder und einen Decoder umfassen. Die leistungsstärksten Modelle verbinden den Encoder und Decoder auch über einen Aufmerksamkeitsmechanismus. Wir schlagen eine neue einfache Netzwerkarchitektur vor, den Transformer, der ausschließlich auf Aufmerksamkeitsmechanismen basiert und vollständig auf Rekurrenz und Konvolutionen verzichtet. Experimente mit zwei maschinellen Übersetzungsaufgaben zeigen, dass diese Modelle qualitativ überlegen sind, während sie parallelisierbarer sind und deutlich weniger Zeit zum Trainieren benötigen. Unser Modell erreicht 28,4 BLEU bei der WMT 2014-Übersetzungsaufgabe Englisch-Deutsch und verbessert damit die bestehenden besten Ergebnisse, einschließlich Ensembles, um über 2 BLEU. Bei der WMT 2014-Übersetzungsaufgabe Englisch-Französisch erreicht unser Modell nach 3,5 Tagen Training auf acht GPUs einen neuen, hochmodernen BLEU-Score von 41,8 für ein einzelnes Modell, ein kleiner Bruchteil der Trainingskosten der besten Modelle aus der Literatur. Wir zeigen, dass sich der Transformer gut auf andere Aufgaben übertragen lässt, indem wir ihn erfolgreich auf die englische Wählerschaftsanalyse sowohl mit großen als auch mit begrenzten Trainingsdaten anwenden.

Erläutern: Die dominanten Sequenztransduktionsmodelle

Beantworten Sie die Frage zum Papier, nachdem Sie es sorgfältig gelesen haben.

Um zu beurteilen, ob der Transformer auf andere Aufgaben verallgemeinert werden kann, haben wir Experimente zur englischen Wählerschaftsanalyse durchgeführt. Diese Aufgabe stellt besondere Herausforderungen dar: Die Ausgabe unterliegt starken strukturellen Einschränkungen und ist deutlich länger als die Eingabe. Darüber hinaus konnten RNN-Sequenz-zu-Sequenz-Modelle in kleinen Datenmengen keine hochmodernen Ergebnisse erzielen.

Wir präsentieren ein hochmodernes Spracherkennungssystem, das mithilfe von End-to-End-Deep-Learning entwickelt wurde. Unsere Architektur ist deutlich einfacher als herkömmliche Sprachsysteme, die auf mühsam konstruierten Verarbeitungspipelines basieren; diese herkömmlichen Systeme neigen auch dazu, in lauten Umgebungen schlecht zu funktionieren. Im Gegensatz dazu benötigt unser System keine von Hand entworfenen Komponenten, um Hintergrundgeräusche, Nachhall oder Sprechervariationen zu modellieren, sondern lernt direkt eine Funktion, die gegenüber solchen Effekten robust ist. Wir benötigen kein Phonemwörterbuch und nicht einmal das Konzept eines „Phonems“. Der Schlüssel zu unserem Ansatz ist ein gut optimiertes RNN-Trainingssystem, das mehrere GPUs sowie eine Reihe neuartiger Datensynthesetechniken verwendet, mit denen wir effizient eine große Menge unterschiedlicher Daten für das Training erhalten können. Unser System namens Deep Speech übertrifft zuvor veröffentlichte Ergebnisse auf dem umfassend untersuchten Switchboard Hub5'00 und erreicht einen Fehler von 16,0 % im gesamten Testsatz. Deep Speech kommt auch mit anspruchsvollen, lauten Umgebungen besser zurecht als weit verbreitete, hochmoderne kommerzielle Sprachsysteme.Collapse

Erstellen Sie eine kurze, prägnante Zusammenfassung des Papiers auf der Grundlage seiner Zusammenfassung.

Few-Shot-Learning (FSL) ist einer der wichtigsten zukünftigen Schritte im maschinellen Lernen und erregt viel Aufmerksamkeit. In diesem Papier konzentrieren wir uns auf das FSL-Problem des Dialogverständnisses, das zwei eng miteinander verbundene Aufgaben umfasst: Absichtserkennung und Slot-Füllung. Es hat sich gezeigt, dass das Dialogverständnis stark vom gemeinsamen Lernen der beiden Unteraufgaben profitiert. Allerdings wird ein solches gemeinsames Lernen in den Few-Shot-Szenarien zu einer Herausforderung: Einerseits erschwert die Spärlichkeit der Stichproben die Modellierung der Verbindung zwischen den beiden Aufgaben erheblich; andererseits ist die Frage, wie mehrere Aufgaben in der Few-Shot-Umgebung gemeinsam gelernt werden können, noch weniger erforscht. Als Antwort darauf stellen wir FewJoint vor, den ersten FSL-Benchmark für gemeinsames Dialogverständnis. FewJoint bietet ein neues Korpus mit 59 verschiedenen Dialogdomänen aus echten industriellen APIs und eine Code-Plattform zur Vereinfachung des Aufbaus von FSL-Experimenten, die die Forschung in diesem Bereich voraussichtlich voranbringen werden. Darüber hinaus stellen wir fest, dass eine unzureichende Leistung der Few-Shot-Einstellung häufig zu einem verrauschten Teilen zwischen zwei Teilaufgaben führt und das gemeinsame Lernen stört. Um dies zu beheben, leiten wir den Slot mit expliziten Absichtsinformationen und schlagen einen neuartigen Trust-Gating-Mechanismus vor, der Absichtsinformationen mit geringer Vertrauenswürdigkeit blockiert, um ein qualitativ hochwertiges Teilen zu gewährleisten. Außerdem führen wir eine auf Reptilien basierende Meta-Lernstrategie ein, um eine bessere Generalisierung in ungesehenen Few-Shot-Domänen zu erreichen. In den Experimenten bringt die vorgeschlagene Methode erhebliche Verbesserungen bei zwei Datensätzen und erreicht eine neue Leistung auf dem neuesten Stand der Technik.

1. Harmony: The harmony in music can be considered a part of its melodic system, but in music theory, a separate focus is often given to harmony with a particular emphasis on:

  a. Chord progression: In music, a separate focus is often given to harmonic developments that feature a connection to one or more of the following: the number of pitches that can be played at the same time, and in music, a pitch and its accompanying pitch discussed together under:

  b. Chord-type: In music, compositions and recordings that use the word "arrangement" (implying different arrangements of the same song) often make reference to the fact that the specific arrangement of the harmonies is engaging, interesting, etc.

  c. Harmonic rhythm: Harmonic rhythm is a concept in music, which refers to the rhythm of harmonic change. It is an aspect of the overall harmonic and non-harmonic elements (see: https://www.thesphere.com/m/music/g/harmony) as harmonic rhythm is a fundamental element in music.

  d. Harmonic complexity: "Harmonic complexity" is a term used to refer to the complexity of harmonies in terms of their harmonic form, the number of layers of harmonism, and the duration for which they are considered, as well as the subjective perceptions that result from these, especially as pertains to connotations and the capacity for a harmony to be pushed further from its harmonic boundaries of norm.

  e. Non-musical theory: Harmonanship, while usually discussed as a standalone subject in music (like in music schools and communities as a formal field of study), music also touches on some other elements as well, such as:

  - Connotations (music for notation, emotion, etc.)
  - Physics (music and physics, harmonies, timbre, etc.) 
  - Academic approach (music and music education)

Geben Sie dem Gericht anhand der Zutaten und Anweisungen einen Namen.

ZUTATEN:
2 (5 oz) Dosen Bumble Bee® Solid White Albacore Tuna, abgetropft
1 Avocado
2 EL Sriracha
1 EL Dijon-Senf
2 bis 3 EL Sellerie, gehackt
2 EL rote Zwiebel, gehackt
2 Frühlingszwiebeln, gehackt
1 EL frischer Koriander, gehackt
Salz und Pfeffer nach Geschmack
2 gehäufte Tassen grüner Blattsalat
1 Tasse Karottenstifte
4 (10 Zoll) Vollkorntortillas
ANLEITUNG:
Thunfisch und Avocado in einer mittelgroßen Schüssel zerdrücken, bis sie gut vermischt sind. Restliche Zutaten zusammen mit Salz und Pfeffer hinzufügen und gut vermischen.
Zum Anrichten jede Tortilla mit einer halben Tasse Blattgemüse und einer viertel Tasse Karottenstiften belegen und die Thunfischmischung gleichmäßig auf die Wraps verteilen. Die Tortilla fest aufrollen, in Scheiben schneiden und genießen!

Peter Munk is a 85-year old Canadian businessman and founder of Barrick Resources, a mining company. He is also the founder and owner of the Munk Debates, an annual public debate where 3 topics are debated, with 500 people in attendance (in Toronto). The topics are "of moral and practical concern". The second debate in 2012 was held on January 12. The theme was "Is there a renewable energy future?"
The four speakers of the debate were: (1) William N. Pentland, (2) Brian Jennings, (3) Margaret W. MacMillan, (4) Al Gore.
- (1) Pentland: the future of the world is renewable, we need to have a long perspective, and we know the technology for renewable energy, and it is just a matter of time.
- (2) Jennings: renewable energy is an act of faith, and the proponents fail to mention the rate and the cost.
- (3) MacMillan: a historian, and she said that history, as a science, stands aside when a better argument is put forth by a philosopher: "We have not an answer to Mr. Gore, we can only say, as a historian, that this is the most govenrment-intensive set of solutions I have ever heard of."
- (4) Gore: this is a battle between right and wrong. The 1% vs. The 99% plus the planet. This is a moral issue of a momentous kind, and it is also a legal issue. Why do we have government? To keep the peace, to provide environmental security, and the issue of the environment, from which all other issues spring, is the most important. It is a legal responsibility and we fail unless we have clean air and clean water. It is a moral issue: to raise boys and girls with the understanding that they have to lower their carbon footprint. It is an economic issue: clean energy is 3 times as job intensive and it is a resource. It is a national security issue, and a personal one: when I lost my daughter, I realized that the most important thing is to talk to your children, to teach them as much as you can, because one day you will die, and they will need to know, and I learned to appreciate the beauty of the planet. The issue is a Kantian imperative, to think in terms of the impact on others, others whose lives are being sacrificed for the lives that we are privileged to lead. We are a net producer, and we have to live our lives, but we have an obligation, and the promises of the others, to protect the environment.

An effective communication system is one that is open, honest, and transparent. Clear and transparent communication, especially in the workplace, helps to prevent conflicts as well as to resolve any conflicts that may arise.

If a business wants to maintain a good working environment, it is best to encourage a workplace culture that is open, honest, and transparent. instruction: Welche möglichen Auswirkungen hat die Verwendung einer Einweg-Plastikflasche im Vergleich zu einer Mehrwegflasche auf die Umwelt und die menschliche Gesundheit?

instruction: Erklären Sie den Prozess der natürlichen Selektion und wie er zur Evolution und Anpassung von Arten beiträgt.
output:
Natural selection is the process in which organisms or factors associated with a particular species interact and determine the probability of each possible genotype existing in a species, often through the natural and natural history of their phenotypic traits. The long-term operation of natural selection, also known as selection, is based on the differential effect of the variability and heterogeneity of associated factors in determining the probability of the occurrence of similar traits in a species.

The natural and natural history of the factors associated with a particular trait are important factors for the evolution of the trait and its course. Natural history is often a key factor, as these factors are, in many cases, the primary driver of the evolution of a particular trait.

The evolution of a species, as the term given for an event in the history of life, is the result of the prior factors influencing the trait variability of a species. The process of natural selection, therefore, is a crucial factor in determining the evolution of traits and their importance for the ongoing and unprocessed events of biological adaptation.

The various factors and processes involved in biological adaptation through natural selection can be examined over short timescales, as the operation of organisms and their characteristics in a particular species is, to a large extent, subject to short-term influences. Short-term events may be more or less high-impact, but the impact of the factors determining the probability and contribution of associated traits cannot be estimated without understanding the mechanisms involved, as the many and varied factors are usually interrelated.

The two fundamental aspects involved in the study of biological adaptation are the modification and the distribution of trait variation. The ongoing and uncontrolled natural development processes are governed by these two key features.

Natural selection and adaptation refer to the general concepts in the biological science, but no specific hypotheses arise, as the previous few centuries of biological research (since the development of the scientific method) have provided a sufficient empirical understanding of the fundamental aspects of biological adaptation. The effects of natural and natural history are well understood, and the relevant knowledge and understanding can be gathered, taught, and learned. The following qualifications are not significantly different from the general knowledge in the field of biological science.

Evolution, natural selection, and adaptation are highly interrelated in the study of biology. The mechanisms involved, however, are usually studied under the context of these general terms, which is usually reflective of the field as a whole.

## Evolution and Natural Selection: The Importance of Starting a Research Project

If the Internet had been invented during the Renaissance, it is this rich material that would provide a clear basis for the development of the literature of the period. This is not to say that there is no literature from the time that is Internet-related. The fields of science look upon us as their slaves, and expect us to serve them. Science without religion is blind, religion without science is lame. Let us see if we cannot work out a religion of Theism, using Science as our only guide.

This is a religion, based on science, with no idols, without sacrifice, and with no priest but yourself. It contains all the good in church, state, and utopia, and rejects what is cruel, inhuman, and unjust. Follow your reason as your prophet, and a thousand times around this globe and back again, will it lead you to the Chrisrian's God.

I have framed this course of faith in a scientific manner. I have it all, and I can make my experiment in a letter. I will send it to you, if you will only help me.

Dear Editor: Science is blind, but the helios, the sun, gives us light. Let us see if science will lead us to the light of a God.

The writer, a student at Columbia University, is struggling with his classes, especially those in science. He asks if the science of the future will be able to provide a religion to sustain him. His paper is a pamphlet, "The Method of Nature" (New York: D. Appleton, 1901), promoting his "scientific religion" based on "orthic" or "Ophitic" Christianity (masonry), and evolution. The text claims that all must believe in a God, for they need some conditions for their religion. He writes as he can, having no argument for his claimed 184 pages. The book is a collection of thoughts, not an argument. Most of the pamph is reprinted in a summary, with much editing, in the text, which also contains some unique passages.

The student's musings are directed to the future, when the world will be at rest, with the religion of the sun. He writes, "To-morrow" is the title of his pamphlet, "I have given you a faith, and what is the tomorow (sic) of religion?" (p. 31). He asks, "Is it not possible that in the twentieth century they will be a Christ, a God, like our Christ?" (p. 49). He also writes, "Time cannot be without religion" (p. 10), "All men... All want religion" (p. 13), "Will man cease to pray?" (p. 16), and "Every man... Will have a religion" (p. 17). He concludes, "This is the religion of the future" (p. 34), "This is the religion of the world to come" (p. 47), "The future is with science" (p. 51), and, "The future is found in (science and its religion)" (p. 52). Yet, he also says, "I have not, and cannot, then, prove that there is a God" (p. 29), "I believe in the unity of God, but I cannot prove it"
